separately based on the available container 
sizes (100 mL, 250 mL, 500 mL). Th is system
provides a greater degree of ﬂ exibility in the
amounts of dextrose and amino acids that
can be given. Another advantage of the two-
in-one system is that formulas containing
only dextrose and amino acids are clear, and
any precipitate can be observed. A disadvan-
tage of the two-in-one system is the need for
an additional administration set (intravenous
tubing and other devices required for the de-
livery of parenteral nutrition) for the lipids.
Th e three-in-one system requires a single 
administration set, which saves nursing
time and reduces costs. On the other hand,
the addition of lipids with the three-in-one 
system results in an opaque solution, which
obscures precipitate and increases the risk 
of particulate being infused into the patient.
Addition of lipid into the three-in-one solu-
tion limits the electrolytes and ﬁ nal concen-
tration of amino acids in solution.
